text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak and King Juan Carlos of Spain will hold talks in Cairo starting on Tuesday. The king will be accompanied by his wife on the three-day visit. King Juan Carlos will give a speech on economic cooperation between the two countries during a lunch with Egyptian businessmen.
- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri will today head a meeting of the ministerial committee to develop tourism in Egypt.
The committee to invest in tourism will discuss setting up 85 projects worth 4 billion pounds.

- Cabinet to discuss a plan requested by President Mubarak on Egypt in the 21st century. It forecasts annual per capita income at $3,100 in the year 2017, making available 11 million job opportunities, and increasing the trade volume.
- Mubarak and U.S. President Bill Clinton will meet in Washington starting from March 10. They will discuss strengthening economic ties with American and Egyptian businessmen.
- Egypt starts producing oil for the first time from the Qatara depression in the Western desert at an average daily rate of 3,800 barrels of crude.
- Agricultural projects exempt from taxes and fees in Upper Nile river programme to stimulate development. No taxes on industrial, tourism and minerals projects for 20 years.
- International Monetary Fund Assistant Director for the Middle East Mohammad Arian says that there is huge interest in world financial markets to invest in Egypt.
- New public works and water resources minister to be named in the next few days after the death in November of Abdel-Hadi Radi.
